sentences.text:
This criminal appeal under Section 374(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 has been preferred by the appellant, being aggrieved of the judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 07.08.2015 passed by the learned First Additional Sessions Judge, Sidhi, District Sidhi (M.P.)
in Sessions Trial No. 200/2013, whereby the appellant was convicted under Section 3/4 of Prevention of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for life along with a fine of Rs. 20,000/-, with default stipulation.
6.

sentences.text:
The prosecution story, in brief, is as under:-
6.1
According to the complainant/mother of the victim on 22.07.2014, around 10:00 a.m., she was threshing straw in a field near Raha.
Her 5- year-old daughter (the prosecutrix) was playing nearby.
At that time, the accused, Vipin (a village resident), picked up the child.
Believing he was simply feeding her, the complainant continued working.
Accused Vipin took the child inside the house and raped her.
The complainant/mother heard cries, entered the house, and saw Vipin flee.
The prosecutrix was bleeding profusely, with bloodstains on her frock and scarf.
The complainant/mother carried her daughter home and informed Mathura Prasad Vaishya, Ayodhya Prasad Vaishya, Rajendra Prasad, and Umesh Kumar Vaishya.
That evening at 6:00 p.m., she lodged a report at the police station.
Police registered FIR No. 267/2014 under Section 376 of the IPC and Sections 3/4 of the POCSO Act, 2012.
They medically NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:16127 3 CRA-3814-2017 examined the prosecutrix, recorded witness statements, and arrested the accused based on prima facie evidence.
The investigation confirmed penetrative sexual assault.
A charge sheet was filed under the same sections.
6.2 At trial, the appellant denied the charges and claimed false implication.
Based on the prosecution's evidence and witness testimony, the trial court convicted and sentenced the appellant as detailed above.
The appellant has now filed this criminal appeal.
7. Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the trial court erred in law and fact by convicting the appellant under Sections 3 and 4 of the POCSO Act.
The court failed to properly evaluate the evidence.
The prosecution did not prove the appellant's guilt beyond reasonable doubt, as required in criminal cases.
In addition, the appellant was falsely implicated due to prior enmity, a key factor that the trial court ignored.
The sentence is harsh, excessive, and disproportionate to the facts.

He,
therefore, prayed that the impugned judgment of conviction and sentence be set aside and appellant be acquitted from the aforesaid charge.
8 . Per contra, counsel for the State submitted that the appellant's conviction under Sections 3 and 4 of the POCSO Act is legal and proper.
The trial court has correctly appreciated the evidence and applicable law, as the prosecution proved all ingredients of penetrative sexual assault under Section-3.
The defence's plea of false implication lacks cogent evidence.

The investigation was fair and lawful, causing no prejudice to NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:16127 4 CRA-3814-2017 the accused.
Accordingly, the appeal deserves to be dismissed.

9. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the trial court.

sentences.text: To bring home the charges, the prosecution examined as many as 12 witnesses.
11. PW-2-the victim's mother, testified that the incident occurred around 10:00 a.m., roughly two months before her deposition.
She had left her old house to dispose of cow dung in the field, leaving her daughter playing nearby.
Upon returning, she found the victim lying on a cot, blood oozing from her private parts, and crying in severe pain.
That day, accused Vipin Vaishya had visited the house and was playing with the victim.
PW-2 called her sister-in-law for help, convened a panchayat with Chhotelal, Munna, Santosh, Ghinha, Umesh, Bablu, and others, then proceeded to the police station (her husband being away for work).
She filed FIR Exhibit P-3, after which the victim was taken to Rewa for medical examination.
In para 9 of her cross-examination, she denied the suggestion that the accused committed no offense against her daughter.

12. Mathura Prasad Vaishya (PW-1), Rajendra Prasad Vaishya (PW- 3), Umesh Kumar Vaishya (PW-4), and Ayodhya Prasad Vaishya (PW- 5) testified that the victim's mother told them that accused Vipin, had raped her daughter.
They also stated that when they went to the victim's house, they saw her bleeding heavily from her private parts.

These witnesses further testified that the police seized blood, dirt, and other NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:16127 5 CRA-3814-2017 evidence from the scene in his presence and prepared a seizure memo (Exhibit P-1).

13. Ram Milan Prajapati (PW-7), the Patwari posted in Tehsil Rampur Naikin for Village Maun,
stated that on 06.08.2013, he received instructions from Rampur Naikin Police Station to prepare a spot map of the crime scene (Exh. P/9), which he did.
14.
R. R. Mishra (PW-6), the then Sub-Inspector at Rampur Naikin Police Station, testified that on 22.07.2013, the victim's mother verbally reported the incident at the station.

He registered FIR (Ex.
P-3) against the accused under Section 376 IPC and Sections 3/4 POCSO Act.
He prepared the medical examination form (Ex. P-4), obtained parental consent, and sent the victim to Community Health Centre, Rampur Naikin, via constable Sainik Lalbhai Chandan.
At the scene, he seized bloodstained soil (seizure memo Ex. P-1) and prepared the site map (Ex. P-2).

and semen slide (seizure memo Ex. P-4A).

Dr. Pushpa Bhagat (PW-8)
examined the victim on 27.07.2013 and found injuries, including active bleeding from her private parts and an abrasion below the navel.
This corroborates the mother's account.
The absence of human sperm in the forensic report is immaterial, as the doctor's findings confirm recent injury and bleeding consistent with rape.

Thus, the prosecution has proved beyond reasonable doubt that the accused raped the victim and as such, we are of the considered opinion that the trial court has rightly convicted the appellant under Section 3/4 of the POCSO Act and as such, no error is found in the judgment passed by the trial court.
